content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Secondary efficacy endpoints lack stated analysis methods",
      "quote": "The secondary endpoints are: Efficacy: • Proportion of patients achieving EASI-50, EASI-75, and EASI-90 ...",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol lists multiple secondary efficacy endpoints (e.g., EASI-50/75/90, IGA, pruritus NRS) but does not specify the statistical analysis methods for these endpoints. Only the primary endpoint analysis is described in Section 10.4.3.1.",
      "fix": "Add a subsection under Statistical Methods that describes the analysis for each secondary efficacy endpoint, including model, covariates, and handling of missing data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint in the study is the percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16.",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint definition lacks a full estimand specification: population (FAS is stated later, but not here), variable (percent change in EASI), intercurrent events (e.g., rescue medication, discontinuation) are not defined, and summary measure (e.g., mean difference) is not stated in the endpoint definition.",
      "fix": "Provide a complete estimand for the primary endpoint, including handling of intercurrent events and the summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "No analysis specified for immunogenicity objective",
      "quote": "To assess the immunogenicity of REGN3500 in adult patients with moderate-to-severe AD",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "2.2 Secondary Objectives",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The immunogenicity objective is listed as a secondary objective, but no corresponding endpoint or analysis is described in the endpoints or statistical methods sections.",
      "fix": "Add immunogenicity endpoints (e.g., anti-drug antibody incidence) and their analysis methods."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoints not defined",
      "quote": "Any exploratory endpoints will be described in the statistical analysis plan (SAP).",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The exploratory objectives mention biomarkers, QOL, pain, and sleep, but no exploratory endpoints are listed in the protocol; they are deferred to the SAP. This is a gap in the protocol's completeness.",
      "fix": "List the exploratory endpoints in the protocol or provide a timeline for SAP finalization before study start."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data",
      "quote": "For continuous variables, descriptive statistics will include the following information: the number of patients reflected in the calculation (n), mean, SD, median, first quartile (Q1), third quartile (Q3), minimum, and maximum.",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "10.4 Statistical Methods",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical methods section does not describe how missing data will be handled for the primary or secondary efficacy analyses. This is a critical gap for a confirmatory trial.",
      "fix": "Specify the primary method for handling missing data (e.g., multiple imputation, mixed model repeated measures) and sensitivity analyses."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size does not account for dropout",
      "quote": "the enrollment of 60 patients per treatment group will provide 96% power to detect a 35% difference ...",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "10.2 Justification of Sample Size",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size justification does not mention any adjustment for dropout or missing data. The power calculation assumes 60 completers per group, but if dropout occurs, power will be lower. The protocol should state whether the sample size is inflated for expected dropout.",
      "fix": "State the assumed dropout rate and adjust the sample size accordingly, or clarify that 60 is the number of completers."
    },
    {
      "title": "Hierarchical testing procedure not fully specified",
      "quote": "a hierarchical procedure from high to low dose will be performed for the primary endpoint and selected secondary efficacy endpoints (eg, EASI-75, IGA score of 0 or 1 and a reduction from baseline of ≥2 points responder at week 16) across the REGN3500 dose regimens vs placebo. The final hierarchy will be provided in the SAP",
      "page": 65,
      "section": "10.1 Statistical Hypothesis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The hierarchy is only partially specified; the exact order of endpoints and doses is deferred to the SAP. This could lead to ambiguity in multiplicity control.",
      "fix": "Provide the full hierarchy in the protocol or at least a clear outline of the testing order."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary analysis of the study may affect final analysis",
      "quote": "The assessment of primary and secondary endpoints specified in Section 4.2.1 and Section 4.2.2 performed during the analysis will be the final analysis of the primary endpoint and secondary endpoints. Hence there will be no need for alpha adjustment due to the primary analysis of the study.",
      "page": 68,
      "section": "10.4.3.1 Primary Analysis of the Study",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The statement that the primary analysis will be the final analysis and no alpha adjustment is needed is questionable. If the primary analysis is performed at an interim time, it may be considered an interim analysis, and the lack of alpha adjustment could inflate type I error if the analysis is not pre-specified as final. However, the protocol states it is the final analysis, so this is consistent, but the timing of the analysis (when last patient completes 16 weeks) may not be the final analysis for all endpoints (e.g., week 36 safety).",
      "fix": "Clarify that the primary analysis is the final analysis for efficacy endpoints, but safety endpoints at week 36 will be analyzed separately, and ensure no alpha adjustment is needed because it is a single analysis."
    }
  ]
}
